mainTopic: The end of פרק האשה, and the opening of a new פרק on how long a bride's blood is treated as טהור דם בתולים
overview: The amud opens with the last line of an earlier case: a woman is forbidden on her expected day, because a period usually comes on time. A משנה then compares women's blood of בתולים to grapevines that differ in their wine, and the גמרא explains that a woman's blood is a sign that she can have children. After the הדרן closing פרק האשה, a new פרק begins with a משנה about how long a bride's blood is blamed on the wound of first relations and kept טהור. The answer depends on whether she was too young for periods, had reached the age for them, or had already seen one. The גמרא then explains 'until the wound heals' through רב's sign and שמואל's sign. Next, רב and לוי argue about whether relations during the day use up her four nights, and the גמרא learns from this that first relations are allowed on שבת. רבי חנינא and רבי אסי argue about blood that appears only on a later act of relations. Finally, רב rules on a בוגרת, and a story about רבי begins a challenge to him that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: She is forbidden on the twentieth day
steps.stepSummary: The last line of an earlier discussion: the woman is forbidden to her husband on the twentieth day, because a period usually comes at its regular time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And she is forbidden on the twentieth day, because a woman's flow comes at its usual time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the case it was discussing before this section. The woman must stay away from her husband on day twenty, because that is when her period is expected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given is a general rule: a woman's flow (called her 'אורח', her 'way') tends to come on its set schedule. So on the day it is expected, we treat her as if it may come, and she is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Became forbidden (here, forbidden to be with her husband)
Literally 'way'; a polite word for a woman's period
At its (usual) time

steps.whatToRemember: A woman's period is expected to come at its usual time, so she is forbidden on the day it is due.

phrases.english: And she is forbidden on the twentieth day,
phrases.notes: This finishes a case from before this section. 'She' is the woman whose expected days were being discussed.

phrases.english: because the 'way' comes at its time.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנֶאֱסַר יוֹם עֶשְׂרִים, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאוֹרַח בִּזְמַנּוֹ בָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion from before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: On her expected day (the twentieth) the woman is forbidden, since a period usually comes at its set time.

steps.title: Women's virginal blood is like the wine of different vines
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה compares women to grapevines: their blood of בתולים differs in color and amount, just as vines give different wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Women, in their blood of בתולים, are like grapevines. One vine gives red wine and another gives black wine. One vine gives a lot of wine and another gives only a little.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that the blood from a woman's first time with her husband is not the same for every woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses a picture: vines differ in the color of their wine (red or black) and in its amount (a lot or a little). In the same way, women differ in the color and amount of their virginal blood. So no single pattern is 'normal' for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
Virginity; here, the blood at a woman's first time with her husband
Grapevines
Plentiful / meager

steps.whyThisMatters: Since women really do differ, a different color or a small amount of blood is not by itself a reason for suspicion.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Women, in their virginal blood, are like vines:
there is a vine whose wine is red,
and there is a vine whose wine is black,
and there is a vine whose wine is plentiful,
and there is a vine whose wine is meager.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women's blood of בתולים differs in color and amount from one woman to the next, like wine from different vines.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: every vine has wine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says every vine has some wine, and a vine with none at all is a 'דורקטי', a dried-out vine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Every vine has wine in it. A vine that has no wine is a דורקטי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds his view to the משנה. Every vine gives at least some wine, and one that gives none is called by a special word, 'דורקטי'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part of the משנה said vines give different amounts. רבי יהודה adds that 'a little' is never 'nothing'. A vine with no wine at all is in a different group: it is a dried-out vine. In the same way, a woman who has no blood at all is like that dried-out vine, unable to give birth.

keyTerms.meaning: A dried-out, barren vine (the גמרא explains the word in the next step)
Wine

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
every vine has wine in it,
and one that has no wine in it,
this is a 'durkati'.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל גֶּפֶן יֵשׁ בָּהּ יַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to the vine comparison of the תנא קמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every vine has some wine. One with none is a barren 'דורקטי', and so is a woman with no blood.

steps.title: What 'דורקטי' means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the strange word: דורקטי means 'דור קטוע', a cut-off generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A ברייתא taught: 'דורקטי' means 'a cut-off generation'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by explaining the hard word from רבי יהודה in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'דורקטי' is read as two words: 'דור', a generation, and 'קטוע', cut off. A vine or woman like this has no next generation. So the word itself points to being unable to have children.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
A cut-off generation, with no children after it

phrases.english: Gemara:
It was taught: a 'cut-off generation'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains a word from רבי יהודה's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דורקטי = דור קטוע, a line with no children after it.

steps.title: רבי חייא: blood is good for a woman like leaven for dough
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that just as leaven helps dough, blood is good for a woman. This supports the link between blood and fertility.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: Just as leaven is good for dough, so blood is good for a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching that supports רבי יהודה's idea: having blood is a healthy sign for a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaven is what makes dough rise and come alive. רבי חייא says blood plays a similar role for a woman. This backs up the picture that a woman with no blood is like a 'cut-off' vine.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaven, sourdough starter
Dough
Blood (here, a woman's flow)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya taught:
just as leaven is good for dough,
so blood is good for a woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַשְּׂאוֹר יָפֶה לָעִיסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the idea behind 'דור קטוע'.
steps.raayaObject: That blood is a sign of a woman's health and fertility, as רבי יהודה implied
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי חייא comparing blood to leaven in dough

steps.title: רבי מאיר: plenty of blood, plenty of children
steps.stepSummary: A teaching in the name of רבי מאיר says a woman with plentiful blood will have many children.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the name of רבי מאיר: Any woman whose blood is plentiful, her children are plentiful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching on the same idea, this time linking the amount of blood to the number of children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא said blood is good for a woman. This teaching goes a step further: more blood means more children. It is the opposite of the 'cut-off' vine with no wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Plentiful, many
Her children

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא sees a woman's blood as a sign of fertility: no blood is like a 'cut-off' vine, and plentiful blood means many children.

phrases.english: It was taught in the name of Rabbi Meir:
any woman whose blood is plentiful,
her children are plentiful.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר: כׇּל אִשָּׁה שֶׁדָּמֶיהָ מְרוּבִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second supporting teaching that builds on רבי חייא.
steps.raayaObject: The link between a woman's blood and her ability to have children
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in the name of רבי מאיר

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק האשה
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the פרק: 'We will return to you, פרק האשה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק האשה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional line said when finishing a פרק. It marks the end of פרק האשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It is a promise to come back and learn this פרק again. A new פרק begins after it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you', the formula said when finishing a פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'The Woman'.
phrases.notes: 'האשה' is the name of the פרק, taken from its opening word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final גמרא.

steps.title: A bride too young to have periods
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens with a girl who has not yet reached the age of having periods and gets married. בית שמאי give her four nights, and בית הלל say until the wound heals.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A young girl who has not yet reached the age of seeing blood and got married: בית שמאי say we give her four nights, and בית הלל say until the wound heals.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה about a very young bride who has never had a period. The משנה asks how long any blood she sees after marriage is blamed on the wound of the first relations and not treated as נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood from the first relations comes from a wound, so it is טהור. The question is how long we keep blaming new blood on that wound. בית שמאי set a fixed limit of four nights, while בית הלל have no fixed count and say as long as the wound has not healed.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the opening text of the section
A young girl
She reached the age when periods normally begin
She got married
The wound from the first relations

steps.confusionAlert: 'Giving her' nights does not mean she must separate from her husband for those nights. It means the opposite: during that time any blood is blamed on the wound, so she stays טהורה and they may be together.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי' תִּינוֹקֶת שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּהּ לִרְאוֹת
phrases.english: MISHNAH: A young girl whose time to see [blood] has not yet arrived
and she got married

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נוֹתְנִין לָהּ אַרְבַּע לֵילוֹת
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: We give her four nights
phrases.notes: During these nights any blood she sees is blamed on the wound, so she stays טהורה.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: עַד שֶׁתִּחְיֶה הַמַּכָּה
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: Until the wound heals.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי' תִּינוֹקֶת שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּהּ לִרְאוֹת וְנִיסֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the Hadran closed the previous פרק in step 7, a new פרק begins with this משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl too young for periods who marries: בית שמאי say blood is blamed on the wound for four nights, and בית הלל say until the wound heals.

steps.title: A bride old enough for periods who has not had one
steps.stepSummary: Second case of the משנה: the girl has reached the age for periods but has not seen one yet. בית שמאי give only the first night, and בית הלל give until after שבת, four nights.
steps.simpleTranslation: If her time to see blood had arrived and she got married: בית שמאי say we give her the first night, and בית הלל say until after שבת, four nights.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to an older girl who could have periods but has not had one yet. Because she is older, both sides give her less time than in the first case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since this girl is old enough for periods, new blood might really be a period, so the time is shorter. בית שמאי allow only the first night. בית הלל allow up to מוצאי שבת, which is four nights, because a בתולה usually married on Wednesday night.

keyTerms.meaning: The first night, the wedding night
The end of שבת, Saturday night

phrases.english: If her time to see [blood] arrived and she got married

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נוֹתְנִין לָהּ לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: We give her the first night

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: עַד מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: Until the end of Shabbat
phrases.notes: A בתולה usually married on Wednesday, so Wednesday night through Saturday night makes four nights.

phrases.english: four nights.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some have the word in square brackets. Both mean 'four'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with an older girl, who gets less time than the girl in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl who reached the age for periods but has not seen one: בית שמאי say only the first night, and בית הלל say four nights, until מוצאי שבת.

steps.title: A bride who already had a period before marriage
steps.stepSummary: Third case of the משנה: the girl already had a period while living in her father's house. בית שמאי allow only the בעילת מצוה, and בית הלל allow the whole first night.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she saw blood while still in her father's house: בית שמאי say we give her only the בעילת מצוה, and בית הלל say her whole night.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with the strictest case: a girl who has already had periods before her wedding. Both sides give her the shortest time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl who already has periods is the most likely to be seeing a real period, so the time shrinks again. בית שמאי allow only the first act that completes the marriage. בית הלל allow all of that first night.

keyTerms.meaning: In her father's house, meaning before the wedding
The first relations that complete the marriage, which are a מצוה

steps.whatToRemember: Three cases, with less time in each: too young, then reached the age, then already saw. בית הלל are always more lenient: until the wound heals, then four nights, then the whole night. בית שמאי give four nights, then the first night, then only the בעילת מצוה.

phrases.english: If she saw [blood] while she was still in her father's house

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: נוֹתְנִין לָהּ בְּעִילַת מִצְוָה
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: We give her the relations of the מצוה
phrases.notes: Only that first act is allowed. Blood seen after it is treated as נדה blood.

phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: Her entire night.
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'the whole night' (round brackets) and some say 'all of her night' (square brackets). The meaning is the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה with the third and strictest case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl who saw a period before marriage: בית שמאי say only the בעילת מצוה, and בית הלל say the whole first night.

steps.title: The first case applies even if she saw blood
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the first case of the משנה, the girl too young for periods, applies even if she did see blood before marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: And even if she saw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by widening the first case of the משנה. A girl too young for periods still gets 'until the wound heals' even if she did see some blood before her wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might have thought that seeing blood moves a young girl into the stricter third case. רב נחמן בר יצחק says no. For a girl below the age of periods, having seen blood makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows the משנה
And even

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ' אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak says:
And even if she saw [blood].
phrases.notes: He is talking about the first case, the girl too young for periods. She still gets 'until the wound heals'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: וַאֲפִילּוּ רָאֲתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how wide the first case of the משנה from step 8 is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl below the age of periods gets 'until the wound heals' even if she saw blood before marriage.

steps.title: Proof from the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק proves his point. The end of the משנה separates a girl who saw from one who did not, so the beginning, which makes no such split, must apply either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do I know this? Since the end of the משנה separates 'she saw' from 'she did not see', it follows that in the beginning there is no difference either way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks himself where his ruling comes from. He answers by reading the structure of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a girl who reached the age of periods, the משנה makes 'saw' and 'did not see' two separate cases, step 9 and step 10. For the very young girl in step 8 it makes no such split. So the תנא must mean that the first ruling holds whether she saw or not.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?
The end part of the משנה
The beginning part of the משנה
By inference, it follows that
It makes no difference

steps.whatToRemember: A missing split teaches something. If the משנה divides one case by 'saw' and 'did not see' but does not divide the other, the undivided case holds either way.

phrases.english: From where [do I derive this]?
From the fact that [the תנא] distinguishes in the latter clause
between [a girl who] saw and [a girl who] did not see
phrases.notes: These are the second case (did not see yet) and the third case (saw in her father's house).

phrases.english: by inference, [in] the first clause

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא הָכִי וְלָא שְׁנָא הָכִי.
phrases.english: it is no different this way and no different that way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב נחמן בר יצחק's ruling in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that the first case applies even if the young girl saw blood.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The structure of the משנה: only the סיפא separates saw from did not see, so the רישא holds either way.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רב נחמן בר יצחק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא states openly that בית הלל's rule of 'until the wound heals' applies whether or not the girl saw blood before marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught in a ברייתא like this: בית הלל say she has until the wound heals, whether she saw blood or did not see blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an outside teaching, a ברייתא, that says exactly what רב נחמן בר יצחק said. This gives his reading extra support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר יצחק proved his point by reasoning from the wording of the משנה. Now a ברייתא says it outright: 'whether she saw or did not see.' So the young girl's leniency does not depend on her having had no bleeding before marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this (a phrase that brings support)
Until the wound heals
Whether she saw blood or did not see

steps.whatToRemember: For a girl too young for periods, בית הלל's rule of 'until the wound heals' applies even if she saw blood before marriage.

phrases.english: It was also taught in a ברייתא like this:
Beit Hillel say:
until the wound heals,
whether she saw or did not see.
phrases.notes: He means whether or not she had seen blood back before the marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא to back up the logical proof from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim that the first case applies even if she saw blood
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting בית הלל: 'whether she saw or did not see'

steps.title: How long is 'until the wound heals'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's phrase and asks how long that time lasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Until the wound heals.' Until how long?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. The משנה gave no clear time limit, so how do we know when the wound has healed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Until the wound heals' does not give a number of days. A practical measure is needed, because once the wound heals, any blood she sees counts as נדה blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Until how much / how long?

phrases.english: "Until the wound heals."
Until how long?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the wording of בית הלל in the first case of the משנה and asks for a measure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical time limit or sign for when the wound counts as healed

steps.title: רב says: as long as she is נוחרת
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the wound has not healed as long as she is 'נוחרת', a word that the גמרא will explain later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the wound counts as unhealed the whole time that she is נוחרת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives his answer to the question. The answer depends on a hard word, נוחרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a number of days, רב gives a physical sign. But the word is unclear, so the next steps argue about it and then explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: A hard word that רב uses for the state of the unhealed wound; the גמרא explains it below
All the time that / as long as

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
all the time that she is noḥeret.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: As long as she is נוחרת

steps.title: שמואל gives his own measure
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says he does not know the word נחירה. He says the time lasts as long as there is still blood from relations, using polite language.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I told this to שמואל, he said to me: I do not know what this נחירה is. Rather, it lasts as long as the 'saliva' is in the 'mouth' because of relations.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה reports that שמואל did not accept רב's word. שמואל gave a different measure of his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's measure is the blood that relations themselves cause. As long as relations still bring out blood, the wound has not healed. He speaks in clean, indirect language, so 'saliva in the mouth' stands for blood in the body.

keyTerms.meaning: The noun form of רב's word נוחרת
Saliva (here a polite way to say blood)
Marital relations

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'saliva in the mouth' literally. It is a polite way of talking about blood in the body after relations.

phrases.english: When I said it before Shmuel,
he said to me:

phrases.aramaic: נְחִירָה זוֹ אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מָה הִיא,
phrases.english: this noḥeret, I do not know what it is,
rather, all the time that the saliva is found
in the mouth because of intercourse.
phrases.notes: Polite wording. He means as long as relations are still bringing out blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: שמואל sets aside רב's unclear term and offers his own sign.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wound counts as unhealed as long as relations still produce blood.

steps.title: What did רב mean by נחירה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב's word נחירה actually describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The נחירה that רב spoke about: what does it look like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב's word and asks for a clear picture of it. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since שמואל did not know the word, the גמרא wants to know what רב had in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case like? / How do we picture it?

phrases.english: The noḥeret that Rav said,
what is it like?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from שמואל's view to explain רב's term.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical meaning of רב's word נחירה

steps.title: Signs that the wound has not healed
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק heard from רב himself: if her bleeding depends on her position or her seat, the wound has not yet healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said: רב himself explained it to me. If she sees blood when standing but not when sitting, the wound has clearly not healed. If she sees blood when sitting on the ground but not on pillows and blankets, the wound has clearly not healed.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone who heard it straight from רב explains what נחירה means. It means bleeding that comes from pressure or strain on the wound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blood only comes with strain, such as standing or a hard seat, it is coming from the wound. A period would not depend on how she sits. So this blood is still treated as wound blood, which is טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clearly known
Pillows and blankets (soft seats)
The ground (a hard seat)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak said:
to me it was explained by Rav himself:
she stands and sees blood,
she sits and does not see,
it is known that the wound has not healed.
on the ground and she sees,

phrases.aramaic: עַל גַּבֵּי כָּרִים וּכְסָתוֹת וְאֵינָהּ רוֹאָה
phrases.english: on pillows and blankets and she does not see,
it is known that the wound has not healed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 with concrete examples.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bleeding that depends on strain (standing, or a hard seat) shows the wound is unhealed.

steps.title: The sign that the wound has healed
steps.stepSummary: If she sometimes sees blood and sometimes not, no matter where she sits, the wound has healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If on every kind of seat she sometimes sees blood, and on every kind of seat she sometimes does not, then the wound has clearly healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The explanation of רב's word finishes with the opposite case, which tells us when the wound is healed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the bleeding has nothing to do with strain or seat, it is not coming from the wound. So it must be period blood, and her leniency is over.

keyTerms.meaning: On all of them (every kind of seat)
The wound has healed

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, blood linked to strain means the wound is still open. Blood that comes no matter how she sits means the wound has healed and the blood is נדה.

phrases.english: on all of them she sees,
on all of them she does not see,
phrases.notes: He means sometimes she sees and sometimes she doesn't, whatever she sits on. So the seat makes no difference.

phrases.english: it is known that the wound has healed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation with the healed case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bleeding that does not depend on her seat shows the wound has healed.

steps.title: רב and לוי argue about relations during the day
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the second case of the משנה, רב and לוי argue about whether relations during the daytime use up her four nights.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Her time has arrived,' and so on. It was stated: if she had relations during the days, רב says she has not lost her nights, and לוי says she has lost her nights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the girl who has reached the age for periods, who gets four nights. It brings an argument between two אמוראים about relations during the daytime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that relations during the day do not take away any of her four nights. לוי holds that daytime relations count against them and use up her allowance. The reasons for each side come in the next part of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Her time has arrived (she has reached the age for periods)
She had marital relations
She has lost her nights

phrases.english: "Her time has arrived," etc.
It was stated:
if she had relations during the days,
Rav says: she has not lost the nights,
and Levi says: she has lost the nights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the first case of the משנה and turns to the second case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחלוקת: רב says daytime relations do not use up her four nights; לוי says they do.

steps.title: רב and לוי give their rulings
steps.stepSummary: רב says daytime relations do not use up her nights, because the משנה gives a fixed end point of מוצאי שבת. לוי says they do use up her nights.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: She did not lose any nights, because the משנה says 'until the end of שבת.' לוי said: She did lose nights.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives the actual words of רב and לוי in the argument that was just introduced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב points to the משנה's fixed end point, 'until מוצאי שבת.' Because the end point is fixed, having relations during the day does not shorten the time. לוי disagrees and holds that a daytime act counts as one of her four.

keyTerms.meaning: she lost (used up) some of her nights
the end of שבת, Saturday night

phrases.english: Rav said: She did not lose nights;
we learned 'until the end of Shabbat.'
phrases.notes: He is quoting the משנה, which gives a fixed end point for the four nights. The daytime act cannot move that end point earlier.

phrases.english: And Levi said: She lost nights.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two positions in the argument introduced in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: daytime relations do not use up her nights. לוי: they do.

steps.title: לוי explains 'four nights' as four time-periods
steps.stepSummary: According to לוי, the משנה's 'four nights' really means four time-periods, and a daytime period counts too.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the משנה mean when it says 'four nights'? It means four time-periods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how לוי reads the משנה, since the משנה's wording, 'four nights,' seems to count only nights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For לוי, 'nights' is not exact. It means any time-period, whether day or night. So a daytime act uses up one of the four periods.

keyTerms.meaning: time-periods (a day or a night)

phrases.english: What is the 'four nights' that it teaches?
Four time-periods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes לוי's statement from step 21 by giving his reading of the משנה's words 'four nights'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Four nights' would seem to count only nights, which fits רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Nights' means time-periods, so a daytime act counts as one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוי: the משנה's 'four nights' means four עונות (time-periods, day or night), so a daytime act uses one up.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'nights' according to רב?
steps.stepSummary: If רב holds that daytime relations are also part of the allowed time, why does the משנה say 'nights' at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב, why does the משנה need to say 'four nights'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges רב. If daytime is also allowed and does not count against her, the word 'nights' seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the whole span up to מוצאי שבת is allowed, day and night, and daytime acts cost nothing. So why does the משנה bother to count 'nights' at all? The word seems pointless in רב's view, and it is the very phrase לוי relies on in step 22.

keyTerms.meaning: why do I need it? (why is this wording needed)

phrases.english: And according to Rav, why do I need
to teach 'four nights'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending לוי's reading, the גמרא tests רב against the same wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that daytime relations do not use up her nights
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If day and night are both included, the word 'nights' in the משנה has no purpose.

steps.title: 'Nights' teaches proper conduct
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says 'nights' to teach good manners: relations should normally be at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us proper conduct, that the normal way is to have relations at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers on behalf of רב that the word 'nights' is not a legal limit. It teaches proper behavior.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentions nights because that is the proper and normal time for relations. It does not mean daytime counts against her four nights, so רב's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: proper conduct, the decent way of behaving
it teaches us
marital relations

phrases.english: It teaches us proper conduct,
that the way of relations is at night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The wording teaches behavior, not a legal limit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Nights' seemed to mean only nights count.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Nights' just teaches that relations should properly be at night.

steps.title: Why say 'until מוצאי שבת' according to לוי?
steps.stepSummary: If לוי reads the count as four time-periods, the משנה could have said only 'four nights.' Why add 'until מוצאי שבת'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to לוי, the משנה should just say 'four nights.' Why does it need 'until the end of שבת'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges לוי. The words 'until מוצאי שבת,' which רב relied on, seem extra in לוי's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For לוי, the count is simply four time-periods, so 'four nights' would be enough. Adding a fixed end date seems pointless, and it is exactly the phrase רב used to prove his view.

keyTerms.meaning: let it teach (it should have said)

phrases.english: And according to Levi, let it teach 'four nights';
why do I need 'until the end of Shabbat'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 23, this time aimed at לוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If only four periods matter, the fixed end point 'until מוצאי שבת' adds nothing.

steps.title: It teaches that first relations are allowed on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The words 'until מוצאי שבת' teach that a husband may have relations with his new bride for the first time on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us that it is allowed to have first relations on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers on behalf of לוי that the phrase 'until מוצאי שבת' teaches a separate law about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four nights run into שבת. By mentioning שבת, the משנה shows that first relations are allowed then, even though they may cause bleeding. So the phrase is not about the counting at all.

keyTerms.meaning: it is permitted
to have relations
here: for the first time

steps.confusionAlert: Here לכתחלה does not mean its usual 'ideally, from the start.' It means the first act of relations with a new bride.

phrases.english: This teaches us
that it is permitted to have first relations on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דִּשְׁרֵי לְמִבְעַל לְכַתְּחִלָּה בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to לוי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The extra phrase teaches a new law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Until מוצאי שבת' seemed to be about counting the nights.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that first relations are permitted on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רב and לוי can explain the whole משנה. For רב, 'nights' teaches proper conduct. For לוי, 'until מוצאי שבת' teaches that first relations are permitted on שבת.

steps.title: Support from שמואל's narrow opening ruling
steps.stepSummary: לוי's ruling matches שמואל, who allows squeezing through a narrow gap on שבת even though pebbles fall.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like שמואל, who said: A person may go through a narrow gap in a wall on שבת, even though this makes pebbles fall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that לוי's ruling fits a known ruling of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going through the narrow gap may knock down pebbles, but the person does not mean to do that, so it is allowed. In the same way, first relations on שבת are allowed even though bleeding may result.

keyTerms.meaning: a narrow opening or gap in a wall
makes pebbles fall off

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general idea: an act that is allowed does not become forbidden on שבת just because some side effect may happen.

phrases.english: Like Shmuel, as Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: פִּרְצָה דְּחוּקָה מוּתָּר לִיכָּנֵס בָּהּ בְּשַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: A narrow opening, it is permitted to enter it on Shabbat,
even though he makes pebbles fall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the law given in step 26 with a parallel ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That first relations are permitted on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's ruling that one may enter a narrow gap on שבת even though pebbles fall

steps.title: No blood the first time, blood the second time
steps.stepSummary: A new dispute: if no blood came at first but blood came on a later act of relations, רבי חנינא says she is טמאה and רבי אסי says she is טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was said: If he had relations and found no blood, and then had relations again and found blood, רבי חנינא says she is טמאה and רבי אסי says she is טהורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new dispute about a bride who bled only on the second act of relations, within her first nights.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether the later blood is from the wound of first relations, which is טהור, or is regular נדה blood, which is טמא. רבי חנינא treats it as נדה blood. רבי אסי treats it as blood from the wound. Their reasons come next.

keyTerms.meaning: ritually impure (like a niddah)
ritually pure

phrases.english: It was stated: He had relations and did not find blood,
and he went back and had relations and found blood,
Rabbi Chanina said: She is impure;
and Rabbi Asi said: She is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the רב and לוי discussion has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא: blood found only on a later act makes her טמאה. רבי אסי: she is טהורה.

steps.title: רבי חנינא's reason: real virginal blood would have come at first
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא rules she is טמאה, because if this blood were דם בתולים it would have come on the first act of relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא says she is impure. If this were really virginal blood, it would have come at the very beginning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the reason behind רבי חנינא's view from the dispute it just introduced. He holds that the late blood is treated as נדה blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No blood came the first time, and blood appeared only later. רבי חנינא reasons that a torn hymen bleeds right away. Since the blood came late, it cannot be דם בתולים, so she is טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood from the torn hymen, which is pure
From the start, at the beginning
Impure; here, treated as a נדה

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina says: she is impure,
for if it really were virginal blood,
it would have come at the start.
phrases.notes: He means the first act of relations, when no blood came at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר: טְמֵאָה, דְּאִם אִיתַהּ דַּהֲוָה דַּם בְּתוּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning for רבי חנינא's side of the dispute stated in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Late blood is not דם בתולים, because virginal blood would have appeared on the first act. So she is טמאה.

steps.title: רבי אסי's reason: like שמואל, the hymen may tear only later
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי rules she is טהורה, since the husband may have had relations without tearing the hymen at first. שמואל said he could do this many times.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי says she is pure. Maybe it happened for this husband the way שמואל described. שמואל said: 'I can have relations several times without blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי אסי's reason and supports it with a statement of שמואל. The late blood can still be דם בתולים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי rejects the assumption that the hymen must tear on the first act. שמואל's statement shows that relations can happen several times without bleeding. So blood that shows up later can still be the pure דם בתולים.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure
It happened (by chance)
Acts of relations

phrases.english: And Rabbi Asi says: she is pure,
for perhaps it happened for him as with Shmuel,
as Shmuel said:
"I can have several acts of relations without blood."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר: טְהוֹרָה, דִּילְמָא אִתְרְמִי לֵיהּ כְּדִשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reason, which goes directly against רבי חנינא's assumption in step 29.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אסי's ruling that late blood can still be דם בתולים
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's statement that he could have relations several times without blood

steps.title: רבי חנינא's answer: שמואל was an unusual case
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that שמואל cannot be used as proof, because he was exceptionally skilled. Ordinary men do not manage this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רבי חנינא, how does he answer? He says שמואל is different, because he was unusually strong.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי חנינא deals with שמואל's statement. He answers that שמואל was an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא does not deny what שמואל said. He limits it to שמואל alone, who had unusual ability. For a normal husband, the first act tears the hymen, so late blood is not virginal.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (how does he answer?)
It is different
His manhood was great; he was unusually skilled

steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא: late blood is טמאה, since virginal blood comes at once. רבי אסי: it may be טהורה, as with שמואל. רבי חנינא: שמואל was an exception.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This means רבי חנינא: how does he deal with שמואל's statement?

phrases.english: Shmuel is different, because his manhood was great.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on the proof from שמואל brought in step 30.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using שמואל as a general model for all husbands
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שמואל's ability was unusual, so it cannot set the norm.

steps.title: רב: a grown woman gets the first night only if she saw no blood
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a בוגרת is given the whole first night. This applies only if she did not see blood. If she saw blood, she gets only the מצוה act of relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב says: a בוגרת is given the first night. This is only when she did not see blood. But if she saw blood, she gets only the מצוה act of relations and nothing more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the rule for a בוגרת, a girl over twelve and a half. רב gives his ruling with a limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a בוגרת may have relations through the whole first night, and blood is treated as דם בתולים. רב limits this to a case where she did not see blood. If she did, only the first מצוה act is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A grown girl, over twelve and a half years old
The first night
The first act of relations that completes the marriage
And nothing more

phrases.english: Rav says: a grown woman,
they give her the first night,
and this applies when she did not see blood,
but if she saw blood,
she has only the מצוה act of relations
and nothing more.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: בּוֹגֶרֶת נוֹתְנִין לָהּ לַיְלָה הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the בוגרת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בוגרת gets the whole first night only if she did not see blood. Otherwise she gets only the מצוה act.

steps.title: Challenge from a story: רבי gave a bride four nights within twelve months
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא against רב. In a real case, רבי gave a bride four nights within twelve months.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged רב from a ברייתא: There was a case, and רבי gave her four nights within twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to challenge רב's ruling. The exact problem is worked out in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב gives a grown woman, at most, the first night. In the story, רבי gave a bride four nights spread across twelve months. During that time she may have reached the age of a בוגרת, so the גמרא needs to check whether the story clashes with רב.

keyTerms.meaning: A real case that happened
Within twelve months

phrases.english: They raised an objection: there was an incident,
and Rebbi gave her four nights
phrases.notes: Both bracketed words mean 'four.' The square-bracket word is the corrected wording, and the round-bracket word is the one usually printed.

phrases.english: within twelve months.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: מַעֲשֶׂה וְנָתַן לָהּ רַבִּי אַרְבָּעָה לֵילוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling from step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a בוגרת gets only the first night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי gave four nights within twelve months, which seems to give more than רב allows. The details are clarified next.

steps.title: What was the case? First option: all four nights while she was a minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the story's case was. It starts testing the first possibility: all four nights fell while she was still a minor.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the circumstances? If you say he gave her all of them during her days as a minor,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks how to picture the story, so it can test each possibility against רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא begins sorting through possible readings of the story. The first option is that all four nights came while she was a קטנה. Rejecting this reading will lead to the real challenge, which continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? How do we picture the case?
If you say (first option to be tested)
The days when she is a minor

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If we say that he gave her
all of them in her days as a minor,

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי? אִילֵּימָא דְּיָהֵיב לַהּ כּוּלְּהוּ בִּימֵי קַטְנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the story from step 33 to see how it challenges רב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to understand the timing of the four nights in רבי's case
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not given yet. The first option, that all four nights were during her time as a minor, is being tested.
